headline: Recommended approval of Certificate of Appropriateness applications at 100 West Canal Street and 183 Main Street; approved May 20 minutes.
summary: Two Certificate of Appropriateness applications were reviewed, for 100 West Canal Street and 183 Main Street. Both were recommended for approval by unanimous vote, and the 183 Main Street recommendation includes three conditions on the porch, posts, and railing. The Building Typologies Final Report was discussed, and no action was taken on it.
decisions: Approved the May 20, 2026 meeting minutes, unanimously.
Recommended approval of Certificate of Appropriateness ZON27-05 for 100 West Canal Street, unanimously.
Recommended approval of Certificate of Appropriateness ZON27-04 for 183 Main Street with three conditions, unanimously.

plain_text:
8/12/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Doug Johnson, Vice Chair; Sue O’Brien; Maggie Hicks
City Staff Present: Ravi
Guests Present: Randy Muth
Call to Order by: Doug
Meeting Start Time: 6:01 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by Sue, seconded by Maggie, to approve the May 20, 2026 meeting minutes.
Voting: unanimous.
Motion carried.
Certificate of Appropriateness Review: ZON27-05 – 100 West Canal St
Randy Muth gave an overview of the project scope. Randy asked about the listing of the building 
on the Local Historic Register even though the building isn’t historic in terms of age. Ravi said 
that the listing of the building is based on survey work done in 2020 which led to the City 
adopting the recommended list of historic buildings for the Local Historic Register, and added 
that Chair Britta Tonn could provide more information. Ravi said that there is a process to 
remove buildings from the Local Historic Register. Randy asked about the benefits to have the 
building on the register. Ravi said that keeping buildings on the register is best practice to 
protect significant historic buildings in the City in the long ter.
Motion by Sue, seconded by Maggie, to recommend approval the Certificate of Appropriateness 
for 100 West Canal Street. Voting: unanimous. Motion carried.
Certificate of Appropriateness Review: ZON27-04 – 183 Main St
Ravi gave an overview of the project, noting that the applicant isn’t in attendance. Ravi said that 
the applicant came to the scheduled July 28, 2026 meeting, and provided details on the 
application with Britta Tonn and Sue O’Brien. Ravi said that no action was taken on July 28, 
2026 because a quorum was not present. Ravi said that the applicant is aware of Britta and 
Sue’s concerns and are willing to address any concerns the board may have, including retaining 
the detailing of the posts.
Doug asked about the roof. Ravi said that the roof is not within the scope of this application.
Motion by Sue, seconded by Maggie, to recommend approval of the Certificate of 
Appropriateness application with the following recommended conditions:
1. The repaired porch should be of a similar architectural style and detail as the existing porch. 
2. The replacement posts should be of a similar profile to the existing posts.
3. The replacement railing should have a similar detail to the existing railing. 
Voting: unanimous. Motion carried. 
Discussion: Building Typologies Report 
Ravi gave an update on the Building Typologies Final Report, and discussed next steps with the 
Planning Commission and the City. Ravi said that the reports provides the city with a baseline of 
how much growth to expect on standard-sized lots in the City. Doug voiced concerns about the 
scaling of three-story buildings with the existing streetscape in the residential areas. Ravi said 
that in the residential district, incremental change over time is likely, and that the consultants 
worked within the 35-foot height limit, which has been the longstanding standard in the 
residential districts.
Doug asked about the placement of buildings behind buildings on longer lots in the City. Ravi 
said that the consultants were not keen about this allowance, and Public Works are not keen 
about the infrastructure impacts. Ravi added that such development potential does allow for 
some property owners access to additional capital, which could help them with retirement 
planning, and that this could help create smaller lots, which could lower purchase prices. Ravi 
said that further discussions with the Planning Commission are needed on the topic.
City Updates
Ravi gave an update on Planning Commission discussions, and on the upcoming 
Comprehensive Plan Open House on August 27, 2026.
Other Business
Motion by: Maggie
Second: Sue
Meeting End Time: 6:56 pm
Adjourn
